items.title: Frosinone Municipality Announces Seven Free Courses at Officine Municipali to December 2026
items.summary: The municipal culture department and Pro Loco will present seven weekly courses in percussion, painting, theatre, visual arts, art history, tailoring and English at the city hall's lower floor.
items.content_html:
AI-assisted summary — A concise view to help navigate news and sources. Learn more

Frosinone's municipal administration has opened a new season of the Officine Municipali, with activities for residents taking shape in the municipal seat at piazza VI Dicembre, on level −2. The programme combines training, creativity, work and socialisation, and is presented as an effort to make culture and the acquisition of new competences accessible to everyone. Within the local news remit for Frosinone and its province, it sits at the intersection of municipal administration and culture in the provincial capital, with a defined public venue and a published timetable rather than a general announcement.

The programme comprises seven free courses: percussion, the Morano painting technique, theatre, visual arts, art history, tailoring and English. Each runs for two hours a week. A presentation is scheduled for 14 October at 17:00, and the courses begin on Monday 19 October, continuing until December 2026. The initiative is promoted by the Comune of Frosinone through its assessorato alla Cultura e al Turismo, in collaboration with Pro Loco Città di Frosinone APS, and was developed with the contribution of Simona Geralico and the municipal offices.

Mayor Riccardo Mastrangeli framed the project in terms of community, saying a city grows also through the opportunities it offers people to meet, learn and put their abilities into play, and describing the Officine as a place where a young person can cultivate a talent, an adult acquire a new skill and people of different generations share experiences and knowledge. Making these courses free, he added, means opening a door and allowing more citizens to take part.

He also said that behind a workstation, a course or a help desk lie concrete needs and personal stories, and thanked Simona Geralico, the municipal offices, the Pro Loco, the teachers and others contributing to the activities. Several practical questions remain unanswered in the published material: no enrolment figures, procedures, capacity limits or number of places are given. The material also does not state the calendar year of the October dates outright, although the courses are said to run until December 2026.

items.title: Cassino Prosecutors Receive Report on Allegedly False Tender Guarantee in Ciociaria
items.summary: A Rome-based firm paid €1,100 for a bid guarantee that checks later found to be false; Carabinieri have reported the head of an insurance brokerage in Cassino.
items.content_html:
AI-assisted summary — A concise view to help navigate news and sources. Learn more

Carabinieri at the Stazione di San Giorgio a Liri have reported the head of an insurance intermediation company to the public prosecutor's office in Cassino, on the investigative hypothesis of fraud, over a surety bond bought to enter a public tender called by a municipality in the province of Frosinone. The case bears directly on the concerns of local news coverage in Ciociaria: a contract tendered in the Frusinate, a payment made against a guarantee, and a documentary check that failed and had to be remedied at further cost. It is, on the available accounts, a procurement matter with a private bidder at its centre.

According to the Carabinieri's reconstruction, the legal representative of a company based in Rome approached the intermediary to obtain a polizza fideiussoria required to participate in the procedure. The company is said to have paid €1,100, plus the prescribed charges, and to have received a document apparently issued by an insurance institution. Verification by the contracting authority, carried out through the competent bodies, is said to have established that the guarantee was false, leaving the company to take out a new bond and absorb an additional expense.

At the close of the inquiries the Carabinieri deferred the brokerage's head to the Procura della Repubblica presso il Tribunale di Cassino. The charge under consideration is, at this stage, fraud. The proceedings remain at the preliminary investigation stage; the woman is to be presumed innocent until any final conviction and may exercise her right of defence.

Several elements remain unspecified. Local reporting notes that neither the municipality that issued the tender nor the total economic loss to the company has been disclosed. Coverage of the case has also pointed to checks available to bidders, including the IVASS register of insurance intermediaries and direct confirmation of a document's authenticity with the company named as its issuer.

items.title: Ciociaro entrepreneur on trial in Cassino over social media defamation post
items.summary: A Sora businessman faces a defamation charge after a post about a former commercial partner invoked Renato Vallanzasca, the complainant's father.
items.content_html:
AI-assisted summary — A concise view to help navigate news and sources. Learn more

An entrepreneur from Sora is on trial for defamation at the tribunal of Cassino, where a social media post aimed at a former business partner from northern Italy is at issue. The disputed message, published after a commercial collaboration ended, is the reason a Ciociaro businessman is answering to a charge heard in the Ciociaria area, making the case a matter of local chronicle as well as a test of how insults posted online are treated by the courts.

The two men had been linked by working relations concerning the purchase of materials, according to the accounts. Those relations broke down, the contacts turned hostile, and the dispute continued on social networks. In one contested message the Sora businessman allegedly urged users to be careful of his counterpart and added a four-word phrase — "Tale padre, tale figlio" — understood as a reference to Renato Vallanzasca, the recipient's father. The recipient reported the post, saying he felt offended by the evocation of his parent.

The complainant, who carries his mother's surname and has built a professional life at a distance from his father's history, was heard before Judge Claudio Fassari. Vallanzasca said in an interview published in earlier years that he had never had a real relationship with his son and had not managed to recover that bond. In May 2026, the company owner reportedly foiled a robbery in Milan, reacting when someone tried to take his watch.

The defendant is represented by the lawyer Sandro Salera; the complainant by the lawyer Stefano Ponchione. The tribunal must assess the content of the post and the context in which it appeared, and decide whether the words amounted to defamation rather than criticism. One account cites article 595 of the penal code and case law holding that offensive material published on a social platform can carry the aggravated form of the offence. No finding has been reached, and the presumption of innocence applies.

items.title: Ferentino-based surgeon listed in Vatican bulletin on Pope's lung operation
items.summary: Professor Elisa Meacci, who leads thoracic surgery at the Gruppo Aditerm in Ferentino, was named in the official bulletin as a member of the team that operated on Pope Leo XIV.
items.content_html:
AI-assisted summary — A concise view to help navigate news and sources. Learn more

Pope Leo XIV underwent thoracic surgery at the Policlinico Gemelli in Rome on Tuesday 13 October, and the team that carried it out included a surgeon working in the province of Frosinone. Professor Elisa Meacci heads the thoracic surgery unit of the Gruppo Aditerm in Ferentino and is named in the official bulletin as a member of the operating team, alongside Professor Stefano Margaritora, who led it. That documented participation is the concrete link between the operation and this territory; the sources report no other local dimension to the case.

According to the bulletin from the Holy See press office, the lower lobe of the Pope's right lung was removed using a video-assisted technique. An extemporaneous histological examination confirmed the diagnosis of pulmonary adenocarcinoma, which pre-operative tests had already suggested. The Pope spent about three hours in the operating theatre for an operation that lasted roughly 90 minutes, the statement said, and it was described as successful and free of complications. He woke normally and returned after a short period of observation to his room on the tenth floor. Margaritora led a team of seven doctors; Meacci, Dr Maria Teresa Congedo and Dr Leonardo Petracca Ciavarella are among those named.

The next morning, the Vatican reported that blood tests and a chest X-ray showed a regular post-operative course, with values within the normal range for that kind of operation. Caution nonetheless remains: one Italian report notes that the results of post-operative examinations will determine whether further therapies are needed and how long the Pope remains in hospital.

The Gruppo Aditerm, described as a health organisation based in Ferentino, said it was particularly proud that Meacci had taken part in an operation of such importance, called her professionalism one of the group's strengths and wished the Pope a prompt and complete recovery.

The Gemelli carries out around a thousand thoracic surgery procedures a year and has worked since 2019 on minimally invasive techniques for early-stage lung nodules, according to one report. That record is background to the case rather than a development for Frosinone.

items.title: Regione Lazio Approves Colfelice Accounts, Cutting SAF Gate Fees and Repaying 91 Municipalities
items.summary: The regional government has validated SAF's 2024-2025 financial plan without corrections, setting gate fees below invoiced rates and triggering refunds to the 91 municipalities that own the Colfelice plant.
items.content_html:
AI-assisted summary — A concise view to help navigate news and sources. Learn more

The Regione Lazio has approved the 2024-2025 financial plan of the Colfelice waste plant in the province of Frosinone without a single correction, and the gate fee charged by its operator, SAF S.p.A., has fallen for the first time in the plant's thirty-year history. Because SAF is owned by local authorities, the change bears directly on municipal budgets and waste charges across the Ciociaria, the province's local-government and environmental brief.

Determination G13258, dated 30 September 2026, set the fee at 232.99 euros a tonne for 2024 and 239.34 euros for 2025. SAF had invoiced 236.95 and 239.53 euros respectively, a gap of about two per cent that it must now return to its 91 member municipalities. TG24.info notes that whether the refund reaches household bills depends on how each authority manages service costs. SAF president Fabio De Angelis said the tariff falls rather than rises and that money returns to member municipalities.

SAF attributes the cut partly to a wider overhaul. It says it ended landfill disposal on 1 January 2024, sending all treated waste to material and energy recovery, against more than a third landfilled in 2022. Operating costs fell from 23.6 million euros in 2024 to 22.2 million in 2025, down 1.4 million, or six per cent. The company also waived the ARERA 'fattore ka' environmental premium, used revenues from recovered materials to lower the tariff and obtained three million euros from FESR Lazio 2021-2027 for modernisation.

Unresolved is the flow of refuse-derived fuel to the Acea incinerator at San Vittore del Lazio. Under current regional rules SAF may deliver only 36,000 tonnes a year, against the plant's authorised capacity of 397,200 tonnes, leaving surplus fuel to be shipped outside Lazio at higher transport cost. De Angelis said the region should apply the proximity principle and keep those flows in the province.

The total refund depends on tonnages conferred by each municipality, figures the material does not provide, and the determination's date postdates the plan period it covers.

items.title: Suspect in Ranucci Bomb Case Answers Rome Prosecutors After Long Refusal
items.summary: Saverio Mutone, who had refused to reply to investigators, was questioned for six hours, while Laura Cianfoni gave witness testimony and a third man remains in Cameroon.
items.content_html:
AI-assisted summary — A concise view to help navigate news and sources. Learn more

Carabinieri and prosecutors in Rome have questioned Laura Cianfoni as a witness in the investigation into the bomb placed outside the home of Sigfrido Ranucci, the former presenter of the television programme Report, according to an exclusive report by Tg1. Cianfoni is described as a person close to Ranucci and was present at dinners with Valter Lavitola, whom the reports identify as a friend of both Ranucci and Cianfoni and who has confessed to ordering the bomb. The device was placed outside Ranucci's home in October 2025 and has been described as a demonstrative attack.

Saverio Mutone, identified as one of the material perpetrators, answered questions for six hours, having until now always refused to reply to prosecutors, unlike other suspects in prison. His lawyer, Carolina Schettino, said the purpose of the hearing was to clarify her client's role. Before the investigators, Mutone maintained that the device was not intended to cause harm and that the bomb was supplied by Gomes Clesio Tavares, described as Lavitola's factotum. Investigators do not at present believe that account.

The position of Tavares himself remains unresolved. He is currently in Cameroon. Although the Rome prosecutors' office has begun extradition procedures, he has broken off contact with his lawyer for ten days, saying he must first settle his own affairs. Reached by telephone, he said he would return only to benefit from any procedural guarantees, reiterating that Cameroon is a country of law and that extradition would take place only if the legal conditions were met.

Ranucci, meanwhile, is preparing to leave Report. He is reported to have said that a twenty-year story is ending and that he would never have imagined such monstrous methods. The accounts do not establish the role of each individual under investigation, and the questioning of Mutone has so far produced a defence version that magistrates in Rome have not accepted.

items.title: Cassino I school stages Prokofiev listening workshop under Atina music project
items.summary: The Cassino 1 comprehensive institute held an auditorium workshop on Prokofiev's Peter and the Wolf as part of the Atina music and culture project, though the two reports give different attendance figures.
items.content_html:
AI-assisted summary — A concise view to help navigate news and sources. Learn more

Pupils at the Istituto Comprensivo Cassino 1 attended a listening workshop on Prokofiev's Peter and the Wolf on Tuesday 13 October, held in the school's auditorium and presented as part of the project Atina, Città della Musica e della Cultura. The event sits within local culture and schools coverage because three concrete elements converge on it: a state school, a named organising association and a contribution from Regione Lazio. Neither report describes effects beyond the school itself.

Five musician-teachers performed live and guided the pupils through the instruments and characters of the symphonic tale, with the pupils identifying the musical themes attached to each figure. TG24.info says 34 pupils took part: classes four and five of the primary school and first-year classes of the lower secondary school Di Biasio.

Radio Cassino gives a different attendance figure of 344 pupils and reports that the school welcomed the project's bando, or call for participation, with enthusiasm. No source reconciles the two numbers, and the discrepancy remains unresolved in the available material.

Both accounts place the workshop inside Atina, Città della Musica e della Cultura, described as ideated and organised by the association LazioCulturaEventi LCE APS and realised with the contribution of Regione Lazio. The school's headteacher, Professor Luigi Abbate, said music was "an extraordinary educational vehicle, capable of stimulating sensitivity, listening and creativity in our pupils". He noted that two of the five musicians were former pupils of the institute, which he linked to the school's music-oriented course, and thanked LazioCulturaEventi, Regione Lazio and the teachers who collaborated.

items.title: Frosinone Council Fails to Elect a President as Centre-Right Splits
items.summary: A first ballot at Palazzo Munari produced no winner after Forza Italia and the Partito Democratico declined to vote and Fratelli d'Italia councillors stayed away.
items.content_html:
AI-assisted summary — A concise view to help navigate news and sources. Learn more

The municipal council of Frosinone failed to elect its president at the first ballot in an extraordinary session on 14 October, leaving the assembly at Palazzo Munari without a confirmed chair. The vote sits at the centre of local administration coverage for Frosinone and its province: it concerns how the city's own council is constituted and who presides over it. The election remains pending, and local reporting cites a 26 October deadline for the resignation of the mayor, Riccardo Mastrangeli.

Only 26 of the council's 33 members were present. The scrutiny produced 12 blank ballot papers, two votes for Angelo Pizzutelli of the Partito Democratico and five for Giampiero Fabrizi of the Lista Ottaviani. Forza Italia and the Partito Democratico did not take ballot papers. Absent were the three councillors of the Marzi list, Domenico Marzi, Carlo Gagliardi and Alessandra Mandarelli, while Armando Papetti was present. Councillors of Un'Altra Frosinone, Anselmo Pizzutelli, Maria Antonietta Mirabella and Giovanni Bortone, also did not collect a ballot paper, nor did the PD's Angelo Pizzutelli and Norberto Venturi.

Three councillors of Fratelli d'Italia — Franco Carfagna, Francesca Campagiorni and Andrea Turriziani, the latter of Polo Civico — did not attend. They stayed away after the party's regional coordinator, Paolo Trancassini, asked the mayor to exclude representatives close to Futuro Nazionale, the party of Roberto Vannacci, from the executive. Forza Italia's group leader, Maurizio Scaccia, said his party would not take part in the vote, in line with the direction of the regional leader Claudio Fazzone. The reference to Vannacci's movement concerns the Lista per Frosinone of the deputy mayor Antonio Scaccia, who is also provincial coordinator and regional head for local authorities of Futuro Nazionale.

A second ballot was expected, with the outcome unresolved and the divisions inside the centre-right majority still open. It is not established when the council will proceed to a decisive vote.

items.title: Anagni Biomethane Site Seized as Capannaccio Works Row Turns Political
items.summary: Prosecutors ordered the seizure of the biomethane plant under construction at Anagni's via Capannaccio after the municipality suspended works on 21 September, drawing opposition demands for answers.
items.content_html:
AI-assisted summary — A concise view to help navigate news and sources. Learn more

A biomethane plant under construction on via Capannaccio in Anagni, on the boundary with Sgurgola, has been placed under seizure — the latest turn in a dispute that falls within local-administration and environmental coverage for the province of Frosinone. The site occupies predominantly agricultural land in the Ciociaria, and the case concerns how the municipality exercised control over the project.

The seizure was ordered by the Procura and executed by Anagni's municipal police through its judicial-police unit, with seals attached. It followed ordinance number 1, signed on 21 September by the head of the municipality's technical service for urban planning, environment and SUAP, which suspended the works. The stated grounds were gaps in the project and authorisation file, including the absence of a prior opinion from the fire brigade and of seismic authorisation, along with missing documents on water disposal, internal and external roads, impermeable surfaces, electrical systems and the connection to the methane network. The scheme is attributed to Società Agricola REM Energia S.r.l., based in Cassino.

Andrea Fiorito, provincial coordinator of the Udc in Frosinone, announced the seizure and said he had previously raised doubts about the regularity of the works. He said he learned of their start about a month earlier from press coverage and reports by residents of via Capannaccio, and that a document obtained through an access-to-records request led him to argue the site could not operate without the necessary authorisations.

The Democratic Party, Sinistra Italiana, the Five Star Movement and Possibile in Anagni accused the centre-right administration of failing to answer questions about the project, calling it a total political failure and, in their words, the real betrayal of the city. They invoked the slogan "never again plants that treat waste on municipal territory".

What the judicial measure alleges, and which offences, if any, are under investigation, has not been disclosed. The seizure is not in itself a finding of criminal responsibility, and the administrative suspension and the judicial step are distinct. Documentary shortcomings had already emerged in January 2025, before the site opened, according to the reporting.

items.title: Frosinone Households Face Surcharges Growing Faster Than Incomes, Uil Study Finds
items.summary: The Uil Lazio and Eures dossier records the province's 2024 average taxable income at 25,517.8 euros, the lowest in Lazio, alongside the region's sharpest rise in Irpef surcharges.
items.content_html:
AI-assisted summary — A concise view to help navigate news and sources. Learn more

A dossier on territorial taxation in Lazio, produced by the regional branch of the Uil union with the Eures research institute, reports that households in the province of Frosinone and its capital carry the region's lowest average taxable incomes while their local surcharges have risen faster. The findings bear directly on the Ciociaria, putting figures on the tax and service bill borne locally.

For 2024 the study puts average taxable income per taxpayer in the province at 25,517.8 euros, the lowest among Lazio's provinces. The average regional Irpef surcharge reached 577.3 euros per taxpayer, up 30.4 per cent since 2019 — the largest increase in the region — while average taxable incomes rose 13.8 per cent. In Frosinone city the municipal surcharge averages 235.2 euros per taxpayer, against 196.3 euros across the province; combined, the two surcharges average 773.6 euros for a provincial taxpayer.

For the municipality of Frosinone, the dossier calculates the two surcharges together at 708.4 euros for a taxable income of 28,000 euros, 939 euros at 30,000 euros and 1,412 euros at 40,000 euros. One account notes that these band figures cover only the regional and municipal surcharges, not the taxpayer's entire Irpef liability.

Other local charges feed into the same household budgets: refuse collection, the water service, property tax, nursery fees and school meals. According to the dossier, their combined cost can exceed 4,600 euros a year for a family on 20,000 euros, roughly 23 per cent of income, and 6,900 euros for a family on 40,000 euros, an incidence above 17 per cent.

Alessandro Cirulli, general secretary of the Uil in Frosinone, said: "Non si può continuare a chiedere di più a chi ha di meno" — one cannot keep asking more of those who have less — describing the matter as "un problema di equità e giustizia sociale" and warning that taxation must not become a further cause of impoverishment for territories already marked by economic fragility and low wages. The union asks the Lazio region and municipal administrations to open talks on easing local taxation and tariffs, through a revision of the Irpef surcharges and measures on the cost of services.

items.title: Stefano Ortolani, Former Jesi Traffic Police Commander, Dies at 58 in Marche
items.summary: Ortolani, who led the Jesi traffic police detachment from 2010 to 2019, died on 13 October 2026 after a month in intensive care following a cardiac arrest.
items.content_html:
AI-assisted summary — A concise view to help navigate news and sources. Learn more

Stefano Ortolani, a former commander of the traffic police detachment in Jesi and an official of the Marche regional traffic police division, died on 13 October 2026, aged 58, at the "Carlo Urbani" hospital in Jesi. Both accounts say he had spent about a month in intensive care after a cardiac arrest, which they attribute to an arrhythmia; the Il Messaggero headline calls it a heart attack while its own text, like Il Resto del Carlino, describes a cardiac arrest. He had undergone heart surgery and a long recovery in 2022.

He joined the traffic police in Ancona as an auxiliary recruit in 1989, moved to the railway police in Milan in 1991 and returned to Ancona in 1993, serving almost twenty years as an inspector. In 2010 he took command of the Jesi traffic police detachment, holding the post until 2019, when he passed the competition for officials and became a vice-commissario at the Ancona provincial command. In 2023 he was appointed to lead the second office of the Marche regional traffic police division. Both reports describe him as a prominent advocate of road safety education, and Il Messaggero says he organised meetings in Jesi schools.

His wife, Barbara, and their children Elisa and Francesco consented to organ donation. The liver was removed at the Jesi hospital in an operation coordinated by the chief physician, Tonino Bernacconi. Thomas Cillo, mayor of Monte San Vito and a fellow police officer, wrote in Italian: "È stato un enorme onore conoscerti. Addio Stefano." The former fencer Elisa Di Francisca posted "Ciao Stefano" with a photograph of the two.

The two reports differ on the mortuary chapel. Il Resto del Carlino places it at the David Icof funeral home in Jesi, in via Salvemini, open from Thursday 15 October between 9am and 7.30pm; Il Messaggero says it opens at the hospital mortuary. Both say the funeral will be held on Friday 16 October at 3.30pm at the Regina della Pace church in Jesi. The family asked for no flowers and for any offerings to go to Iom Jesi and Vallesina Onlus.

items.title: Serrone Stages Second Enduro Fest on Monte Scalambra Slopes
items.summary: The second edition of the Serrone Enduro Fest took place on 11 October, with mountain bikers and e-bike riders filling trails on the slopes of Monte Scalambra, according to the organisers and municipal administration.
items.content_html:
AI-assisted summary — A concise view to help navigate news and sources. Learn more

Serrone held the second edition of the Serrone Enduro Fest on 11 October, giving the slopes of Monte Scalambra over to mountain bikes and e-bikes. The event sits within the local news of Frosinone and its province rather than national sport: a municipal administration took part, and its subject is a mountain trail network. That network, valued, maintained and developed over years by the association Serrone Enduro Park, is described as a regional reference point for off-road two-wheelers.

Spectators, riders and enthusiasts filled the trails and the observation points along the routes. Anagnia described the descents as featuring curves, jumps and technical passages. Brands were present: FRB, Pachamama, Fiuggi E-Bike, Two Wheels and Double3. The mayor, Giancarlo Proietto, the councillor Giulia Atturo and the assessor for sport, Andrea Lucidi, attended, with Lucidi confirming his continued support for the initiative.

Proietto said it was a matter of pride for the whole community to see Monte Scalambra "so alive and welcoming". What made Serrone Enduro Park special, he said, was the spirit behind it: a group of people moved solely by passion for the territory and by "a pure sense of volunteering", who with "elbow grease, love for the mountain and much dedication" were keeping the trails alive and clean and creating "an invaluable resource for the town". He thanked them and the riders present on behalf of the municipal administration.

Mirko Chiappini, the creator and founder of Serrone Enduro Park, said that seeing so many young people and enthusiasts speeding along the trails with a smile was the greatest satisfaction. The park, he said, was born of a pure passion for mountain biking and love for the mountain, and the second edition showed that work carried out over recent years, "often in the shadows and with much voluntary sacrifice", had produced beautiful results. He pledged to continue in the same spirit, to grow the community and the outdoor culture at Serrone.

No attendance figures, race results or timings were released by the organisers or the municipal administration, leaving the size of the field and the competitive outcome unconfirmed.

items.title: Frosinone Council Fails Again to Elect a President as Majority Splits
items.summary: Repeated failures to elect a council president have left Frosinone's chamber without a head for four and a half months, as the centre-right majority weighs an exit from the deadlock.
items.content_html:
AI-assisted summary — A concise view to help navigate news and sources. Learn more

Frosinone's municipal council was due to meet at 18.30 on 14 October 2026 with a single agenda item: the election of the president of the chamber, a post vacant for four and a half months after earlier attempts to fill it failed. A first convocation that day failed for lack of a quorum; only five councillors answered the roll, among them mayor Riccardo Mastrangeli and Angelo Pizzutelli, the senior councillor, who presided. The deadlock concerns the ordinary working of the city's municipal administration.

The majority lacks the 17 votes needed without support from the opposition or dissidents. Fratelli d'Italia and Polo Civico have said they cannot govern with the "vannacciani" — the group of deputy mayor Antonio Scaccia, whose Lista per Frosinone holds two executive posts, including the deputy mayoralty, and four council seats. Scaccia is also provincial coordinator and regional head for local authorities of Futuro Nazionale, Roberto Vannacci's party.

Gianfranco Pizzutelli, president of Polo Civico, said his group would attend to vote for the president. Electing one, he argued, would restore the functioning of the municipality's apex institutional organs, allow an important term to be completed and avert the loss of important development funds; dissolving the executive, he added, opened space for the coalition to recompose. Those who did not vote could not be re-candidates on his list, and Polo Civico would not form majorities with Vannacci's party. Councillors Sergio Crescenzi of Mani Libere and Corrado Renzi of Lista per Frosinone were displeased.

An unconfirmed report concerns a possible step-aside by Scaccia's Lista per Frosinone, which would cost the majority four votes. Under that scenario Scaccia would distance himself politically ahead of administrative elections expected between May and June 2027 and could run for mayor or back a trusted figure outside the centre-right; he could also cite the need to avoid a commissioner takeover and the risk of losing financing or interrupting works. The mayor was said to have met Carlo Gagliardi the previous evening; Gagliardi had been put forward by the mayor himself as a possible presidential candidate, and the votes that then failed were Scaccia's.

items.title: Report records Frosinone's low foreign-resident share and narrowest income gap in Lazio
items.summary: The Leone Moressa foundation's 2026 report on the immigration economy counts 25,246 foreign residents in Frosinone province and the smallest income gap in Lazio.
items.content_html:
AI-assisted summary — A concise view to help navigate news and sources. Learn more

The Fondazione Leone Moressa's 2026 report on the economics of immigration, presented on 13 October, examines foreign residents, entrepreneurship and incomes, and its provincial tables set out how foreign-born residents figure in Frosinone's population, tax base and business ownership. The findings, drawn from Istat, Infocamere and Ministry of Economy data, record the lowest foreign-resident share in Lazio and the region's narrowest income gap between residents born abroad and those born in Italy — measures that bear on the province's demographic and fiscal profile.

At 1 January 2025, Frosinone province had 25,246 foreign residents, or 5.5 per cent of the population, against a Lazio average of 11.4 per cent. Rome recorded 521,761 foreign residents, 12.4 per cent of its population; Viterbo reached 10.6 per cent, Latina 10.1 per cent and Rieti 9.6 per cent. Lazio as a whole counted 651,033 foreign residents, of whom Frosinone accounted for 3.9 per cent.

On incomes, the province counted 23,256 taxpayers born abroad, 7.3 per cent of the total, with an average declared annual income of €15,970 — the second highest in Lazio after Rome. Taxpayers born in Italy declared €22,460 on average, the lowest figure in the region. The €6,490 difference equals 28.9 per cent of the Italian-born average, the narrowest gap in Lazio, with the foreign-born average at about 71 per cent of the Italian-born one. A narrower difference does not necessarily indicate better economic conditions for all: the comparatively low declared incomes of the Italian-born population also weigh on the comparison.

The same pattern appears in Irpef. Taxpayers born abroad paid an average of €2,850, against €4,700 for those born in Italy, about 61 per cent of the latter; across Lazio the ratio falls to 46 per cent.

Entrepreneurship grew faster than the regional average. Frosinone counted 4,225 entrepreneurs born abroad in 2025, 8.5 per cent of all entrepreneurs and 5.2 per cent of Lazio's foreign business owners. Their number rose 14.6 per cent between 2015 and 2025, against 4.9 per cent for Lazio, while entrepreneurs born in Italy fell 2 per cent in the province. In absolute terms Frosinone ranks ahead of Viterbo, with 3,513, and Rieti, with 1,496, but behind Latina, with 5,571, and Rome, with 65,718.

items.title: Ferentino assault: Anagni man robbed of phone at night meeting, husband denounced
items.summary: Carabinieri say a young man from Anagni was struck in the face and robbed of his phone after the husband of a woman he had gone to meet appeared; a suspect reported at liberty.
items.content_html:
AI-assisted summary — A concise view to help navigate news and sources. Learn more

Carabinieri from the Alatri station have reported a man at liberty over an assault in Ferentino in which a visitor from Anagni was struck in the face and deprived of his mobile phone. The incident falls within the province's ordinary local crime coverage: it occurred in Ferentino, was investigated by an Alatri Carabinieri station answering to the provincial command in Frosinone, and was reportedly resolved within hours. The accounts agree on the outline; none adds detail on the identities of those involved.

According to the Carabinieri reconstruction, a young man resident in Anagni had travelled to Ferentino to meet a woman. At about 00:30, the hour reportedly agreed for the meeting, the woman's husband arrived. A confrontation followed and became physical. The man struck the younger man repeatedly in the face, causing visible injuries, then took his telephone and left. The victim managed to get away and telephoned the single emergency number, 112.

A patrol from the Alatri station reached the scene, gave first aid and noted the signs of the attack on the victim's face. He was taken to the emergency department of the San Benedetto hospital in Alatri, where he received treatment and a prognosis of a few days. After taking his formal complaint, the Carabinieri went to the home of the man identified as responsible. There they recovered the telephone taken shortly before and returned it to its owner.

The man was reported at liberty to the judicial authority on hypotheses of personal injury and robbery. One account states that the proceedings remain at the investigation stage and that the reported man must be considered presumed innocent until any final conviction; others note that the accusations against him must be assessed during the proceedings. The supplied material gives no further detail on the inquiry.

items.title: Frosinone inquiry widens as woman is placed under precautionary order over July attack
items.summary: Police in Frosinone have served a third precautionary measure, against a woman accused of obstructing the inquiry into a July attack on a young foreigner that investigators link to jealousy.
items.content_html:
AI-assisted summary — A concise view to help navigate news and sources. Learn more

Police in Frosinone have served a third precautionary measure in the investigation into a violent attack on a young foreigner in the upper part of the city last July. The measure was executed within days of two orders already issued against the two young men described as the alleged perpetrators, extending the case to an accused role in the aftermath of the assault. It falls squarely within the province's local crime coverage, where an inquiry opened in July has now produced three separate measures and a widening set of allegations.

The latest order concerns a woman traced by officers of the Volanti squad on 13 October. She faces an accusation of favoreggiamento, the offence of aiding suspects or obstructing an investigation; investigators say she gave statements they consider false in an attempt to protect the alleged accomplices. She is barred absolutely from approaching the victim, must keep at least 1,000 metres away, may not communicate with him in any form, and is subject to an electronic bracelet.

The underlying episode dates to July and, according to the police reconstruction, arose from jealousy. Two young men, both residents of Frosinone, are alleged to have attacked the victim — one striking him repeatedly with a dog leash, the other wounding him in the back with a sharp object, causing a serious haemorrhage. One was placed under house arrest; the other is subject to an obligation to reside at a given address and to report to the judicial police.

The investigation was carried out by the Volanti and Mobile squads of the Frosinone police headquarters. Officers conducted personal and house searches while medical staff treated the injured man, and the accounts say the alleged perpetrators were identified quickly and the woman's alleged role reconstructed later. The accusations remain at the investigation stage, and the responsibility of those involved must be established in the competent courts.

items.title: Ceccano Charity Walk Raises Funds for Frosinone Cancer League in Serena Ciotoli's Memory
items.summary: Two media reports describe a well-attended memorial walk in Ceccano on 11 October, its proceeds going to LILT Frosinone, with no participant figure or total disclosed.
items.content_html:
AI-assisted summary — A concise view to help navigate news and sources. Learn more

Ceccano in Rosa, a commemorative walk through Ceccano, was held on Sunday 11 October, organised by the SerenaMente association with LILT Frosinone and under the patronage of the municipal administration, in memory of Serena Ciotoli. The event belongs to the local chronicle of the province of Frosinone and the Ciociaria: a municipal initiative that joins local administration, public health and community life, and it matters within that beat because it turns a civic gathering into a call for cancer prevention in the territory concerned.

As reported, the procession left Piazza Municipio, crossed the centre of Ceccano and reached the lower part of the town before returning to the same square. The published reports describe a large turnout and carry the slogan "Prevenire, curare, guarire". Among those taking part were Norbetto Venturi and Elena Di Nicuolo, president of LILT Frosinone. Also present were the mayor, Andrea Querqui, the deputy mayor and councillor for social policies, Mariangela De Santis, and the councillors Cristina Micheli, delegated to health, Gina Carlini, president of the health commission, Federica Maura, president of the Commissione Elette, and Emanuela Piroli, president of the municipal council. The municipal band and cheerleaders accompanied the route, according to one account.

The proceeds from the sale of the commemorative T-shirts were donated in full to LILT Frosinone, the Italian league for the fight against tumours, which took an active part in the initiative. Querqui said the morning had shown how important solidarity and a sense of community are, and that walking in memory of Serena, and of all those who have fought, recalls the importance of prevention, which he called an obligation towards ourselves and those we love. De Santis thanked LILT Frosinone for its participation and contribution, with particular thanks to Elisa, Angela and Cesare. The association said it intended to keep promoting prevention-awareness initiatives.

Serena Ciotoli died on 1 June 2023, aged 26, after fighting a serious form of cancer. No participant count and no total sum raised were given, and the two published reports give no further detail on how the funds will be applied within LILT's prevention work.

items.title: Supino Council Adopts Ten-Year Woodland Plan to Unlock Regional and EU Funds
items.summary: The municipal administration has presented a ten-year forestry management plan that the sources describe as a precondition for accessing European and regional funding for woodland areas.
items.content_html:
AI-assisted summary — A concise view to help navigate news and sources. Learn more

The municipal administration of Supino has presented a ten-year Piano di Gestione e Assestamento Forestale, a forest management and adjustment plan governing the woodland around the town. The development falls within this edition's coverage of local administration and environmental policy, and its reported significance is financial as much as ecological: the sources describe the plan as a precondition for the municipality to obtain European and regional funding. Neither account names Supino's province or places the town within the province of Frosinone.

The document was drafted by the forestry specialist Alessio Arduini. According to the two accounts, it sets out woodland maintenance, the planning of forestry interventions, felling operations, fire prevention and action to reduce hydrogeological risk — pressures the sources describe as particularly sensitive for hilly and mountainous areas. It also aims to protect biodiversity and to preserve the woodland as an environmental resource.

The plan is presented as an administrative requirement rather than a formality. Both accounts state that an updated forest management plan is a necessary condition for the municipality to access funding reserved for woodland areas and the ecological transition. The mayor, Gianfranco Barletta, and the environment councillor, Beniamino Iacobucci, who followed the project, attended the presentation.

Barletta said adoption of the plan did more than actively protect the town's "precious green lung": it opened the way to "important European and regional financing" for woodland areas and the ecological transition. The woodland, he added, would cease to be "a passive resource" and become the centre of a policy attentive to climate change and to tourism and environmental promotion.

What the plan will mean in practice remains undefined. The sources note that its technical contents will determine which areas are affected, which works are scheduled and which funds can be secured, and that the instrument's capacity to turn planning into results will be judged on those points.

items.title: Alatri to Inaugurate Palazzo San Francesco as Base for PNRR-Funded Social Services
items.summary: Stazioni di Posta and Housing Temporaneo, financed by the National Recovery and Resilience Plan, are to find a permanent home in the historic palazzo in Piazza Regina Margherita.
items.content_html:
AI-assisted summary — A concise view to help navigate news and sources. Learn more

The city of Alatri is to inaugurate the new premises of its Palazzo San Francesco presidio on Monday 19 October 2026, with a ceremony scheduled for 18:00 in Piazza Regina Margherita. The building will permanently house two social services and is presented as a strategic reference point for combating social fragility in the area — a municipal welfare project that sits within the administrative life of the province of Frosinone. The services are run by Distretto Socio Assistenziale A of the province of Frosinone, whose lead municipality is Alatri.

Both services — Stazioni di Posta and Housing Temporaneo — were launched by the district together with the Città di Alatri, which acts as capofila, or lead municipality. They are financed through Italy's Piano Nazionale di Ripresa e Resilienza (PNRR) and were developed in coordination with local social services and the Third Sector network.

The stated beneficiaries include people who are homeless or of no fixed abode, migrants, households living in extreme poverty and adults who have lost work. The stated objective is to move beyond emergency shelter: to offer competent listening, a respectful approach and personalised accompaniment, guaranteeing equitable and facilitated access to services and the protection of the rights and dignity of every person.

The project rests on two pillars. Stazioni di Posta is conceived as a stable, accessible and multidisciplinary integrated centre where a person is received, can set out primary needs and build sustainable inclusion pathways with operators. Housing Temporaneo starts from the principle that housing is the first step towards autonomy: it provides short-term reception and accommodation for individuals and families in grave deprivation, accompanied by a team of operators through a personalised plan of recovery and social reintegration.

Several practical questions remain unanswered in the published material. Neither source gives capacity figures for the two services, the duration of the temporary housing, the identity of the operating team beyond a generic reference to a team of operators, whether the inauguration ceremony is open to the public, or whether the services begin operating on the day of the ceremony.

items.title: Frosinone Institutions Gather as Safety Weeks Reach Twentieth Edition
items.summary: Prosecutors, police commanders and labour inspectors joined the ASL's own prevention services for a morning of addresses on workplace and road injury data in the province.
items.content_html:
AI-assisted summary — A concise view to help navigate news and sources. Learn more

The ASL di Frosinone opened the twentieth edition of the Settimane della Sicurezza in the Sala Teatro of its Frosinone headquarters, a provincial public-health initiative that falls within local news for the city and its province. It is promoted by the authority's Dipartimento di Prevenzione, directed by Luciano Figliozzi, and by the Servizio PreSAL, coordinated by Lucilla Boschero, who state the aim of spreading a culture of prevention among workers and in society.

The Procuratore della Repubblica di Frosinone, Francesco Minisci, opened the institutional interventions, stressing the value of inter-institutional networks and the need to strengthen preventive action as a means of protecting citizens and workers. He was followed by the Digos chief commissioner Antonio Pennacchio, the provincial commander of the Guardia di Finanza, Colonel Stefano Boldrini, and the provincial commander of the Vigili del Fuoco, engineer Pietro Giovanni Muscinesi. Boldrini said the question of subcontracts, and the role of safety and control, mattered; Muscinesi said the ministry had provided new practices for managing fires and that his service was glad to take part.

Contributions also came from Alessandra Pezzoli, director of INAIL in Frosinone; Antonella De Prosperis of the Labour Inspectorate; and Simone De Sio, president of the degree course in Tecniche della Prevenzione nell'Ambiente e nei Luoghi di Lavoro at Sapienza Università di Roma. The programme included a reading of injury data that distinguished workplace incidents from those linked to road traffic, so that critical areas could be identified more precisely and interventions directed. De Prosperis said safety was a responsibility for everyone, from employer to worker, and a social responsibility that extended to citizens and motorists.

Boschero said the goal was zero injuries, described as a demanding objective, pursued by sensitising the new generations, including through prevention campaigns in schools. Twenty years, she said, meant a stock of experience, skills and relationships built by institutions, professionals, businesses, associations and workers, and the anniversary was a starting point for new challenges in the world of work. Maria Giovanna Colella, the ASL's health director, said the two decades showed the authority's capacity to build networks and involve institutions, professionals and the productive world in a shared path centred on the health and safety of people.
